profile.headline: I build cloud platforms at enterprise scale — and ship my own SaaS products.
profile.summary: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional and Cloud & DevOps Engineer at TCS with 4+ years in production AWS. I manage 20+ AWS accounts and 2,000+ servers for TCS's client IFF, and outside work I design, build and run four live products on serverpulse.in — observability, FinOps, AI-generated Terraform and an AI terminal agent. Proven record: 80% less manual ops, 60% faster deployments, 20% cloud cost savings.

products.name: ServerPulse
products.description: A multi-tenant server monitoring platform I designed, built and run end-to-end. One lightweight agent per server streams metrics every 10 seconds into live dashboards, with smart alerting, security scanning and a private AI assistant that answers questions about your fleet in plain English.
features: Live CPU, memory, disk, network and GPU metrics pushed over WebSockets every 10s
Smart alert policies with consecutive-breach detection, cooldowns, email / Slack / webhook
AI infra assistant on a local Ollama LLM — metrics and logs never leave your servers
Security scanning: vulnerabilities, open ports, malware, SSH and sudo events
HTTP, service-port, SSL-expiry, PM2 and Docker monitoring with log forwarding
Teams and RBAC, audit log, patching, maintenance windows and an Expo mobile app

products.name: CloudLedger
products.description: Unify, allocate, forecast and optimize cloud spend across AWS, GCP and Azure. A TypeScript monorepo where every surface (explorer, budgets, anomalies, forecasting, reports) reads through one cost-query engine, with a Claude-powered Cost Copilot on top.
features: AI Cost Copilot (Claude): ask about spend in plain English and get anomalies explained
Anomaly detection against a 14-day baseline and 30-day forecasting with weekday seasonality
Virtual tags and shared-cost allocation: even, proportional or weighted showback
Automated optimization actions with approval flow, execution log and one-click rollback
Kubernetes idle cost, RI / Savings Plan coverage, GreenOps carbon and SaaS spend tracking
Pluggable connectors: AWS Cost Explorer, GCP BigQuery billing, Azure Cost Management

products.name: Cloudwright
products.tagline: Describe it. Diagram it. Ship it.
products.description: An AI co-pilot for AWS that turns plain-English requirements into reviewed architecture diagrams and production-ready Terraform. The AI never writes raw HCL: it proposes a typed spec, and a deterministic generator composes vetted, secure-by-default modules.
features: Chat to architecture: AI proposes a typed InfraSpec, rendered as a diagram and a Terraform module tree
Secure-by-default modules: VPC, ALB + EC2, RDS, S3, Redis with encryption, private subnets, IMDSv2
Sandboxed terraform plan / apply in Docker with live WebSocket log streaming
User-defined environments with promotion and isolated state (S3 + DynamoDB lock)
Guardrails: two-person prod approval, per-env spend caps, cost estimates, append-only audit
Multi-tenant companies and RBAC, pluggable AI engine: Claude, AWS Bedrock or offline

products.name: Terminal Agent
products.tagline: Tell your terminal what you want. Approve what it runs.
products.description: An agentic AI platform for the command line. Describe a task in plain English and the agent plans shell commands, rates the risk of each one, runs only what you approve, reads the output and keeps going until the job is done. A team portal runs Claude on the server, so engineers just install one tool and sign in.
features: Agentic loop: plan a command, run it, read the output, self-correct on failure — until the task is done
Two independent safety layers: a local parser and Claude rate every command; the stricter rating wins
Read-only runs instantly, changes ask first, dangerous commands always ask, catastrophic ones never run
Runs in a real PTY in your own shell — colours, prompts and Ctrl-C work; cd and export apply to your session
Secrets masked before anything reaches the model; ai fix diagnoses failures, ai explain breaks commands down
Team portal: device-code sign-in, per-person token metering, monthly limits, pause / stop users and an audit log

journey.intro: From a curious CS student in Bokaro to running 2,000+ servers on AWS at TCS and shipping my own products — this is my story of falling in love with infrastructure, automation and the cloud.

chapters.title: The Beginning — B.Tech CSE
chapters.content: Started my B.Tech in Computer Science & Engineering at Guru Gobind Singh Educational Society's Technical Campus in Bokaro, Jharkhand. From day one I was fascinated by how computers actually work — not just the code, but the systems beneath it. I gravitated toward operating systems, networking and databases, and finished with a CGPA of 8.64/10.

chapters.title: First Real Code — Panicle Tech Internship
chapters.content: Joined Panicle Tech as a Full Stack Developer intern in my final year. I built full-stack applications with React.js and Node.js, designed RESTful APIs, integrated MongoDB and SQL databases, and prototyped ML features for client projects. Managing server deployments taught me that software is only half the picture — the infrastructure matters just as much.

chapters.title: Joining TCS — Cloud Engineer
chapters.content: Graduated and joined Tata Consultancy Services as a Cloud Engineer in July 2022. TCS is where I found my calling: cloud infrastructure and DevOps. I started working with AWS at scale — EC2 fleets, Lambda functions, S3 workflows and RDS databases — and saw how much impact good infrastructure engineering has on an entire organisation.

chapters.title: Building the AWS Management Platform
chapters.content: I designed and built the TCS AWS Management Platform — a full-stack system for managing AWS resources across multiple accounts and environments, with a browser-based SSH terminal, real-time cost analysis, EC2 / S3 / RDS / EKS dashboards, Zabbix monitoring and automated reporting. ~35,000 lines of TypeScript that taught me great platform engineering is about removing friction for every engineer.

chapters.title: Going Deep — First Certifications
chapters.content: Earned the AWS Solutions Architect – Associate and Cloud Practitioner certifications, followed by HashiCorp Terraform Associate. They forced me to understand architecture at a much deeper level. I started leading CI/CD optimisation (60% faster deployments) and a company-wide cost optimisation that saved 20% of monthly AWS spend.

chapters.title: ServerPulse — Building and Launching a SaaS
chapters.content: Outside TCS I designed, built and launched ServerPulse (serverpulse.in) — a multi-tenant server monitoring SaaS. A cross-platform Node.js agent pushes metrics every 10 seconds through Redis pub/sub into live Socket.IO dashboards, covering CPU, memory, disk, GPU, security events, vulnerability scanning, PM2 / Docker and logs. Shipping a product real teams depend on forced me to think about reliability, UX and scale at the same time.

chapters.title: Embracing AI — AWS AI Practitioner
chapters.content: Became genuinely excited about where DevOps meets AI. I earned the AWS Certified AI Practitioner and started building AI-augmented infrastructure tools with AWS Bedrock and the Claude API — cost intelligence, LLM-powered incident response and ML anomaly detection on CloudWatch logs. ServerPulse gained a private AI assistant running on local LLMs.

chapters.title: CloudLedger, Cloudwright & Terminal Agent
chapters.content: Expanded the serverpulse.in family with three more products. CloudLedger is a multi-cloud FinOps platform for AWS, GCP and Azure with an AI Cost Copilot. Cloudwright turns plain-English requirements into reviewed architecture diagrams and production-ready Terraform, with approvals, spend caps and audit built in. Terminal Agent is an AI agent for the command line that plans shell commands, rates their risk and runs only what you approve. All three are live.

chapters.title: AWS Solutions Architect – Professional
chapters.content: Passed the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional exam — AWS's most demanding architecture certification, covering multi-account strategy, migration, cost-optimised and resilient design at enterprise scale. It validates the work I do every day: designing complex AWS systems that are secure, reliable and economical.

chapters.title: What Drives Me
chapters.content: Today I manage 20+ AWS accounts and 2,000+ servers for IFF at TCS, and run four products of my own on serverpulse.in. I'm passionate about systems that make engineers more productive and organisations more resilient — a zero-downtime rollout, a cost optimisation that saves thousands a month, or an AI agent that does the toil safely. My goal is to keep growing as a Solutions Architect and Platform Engineer who bridges cloud, DevOps and AI.
